text:
maya: Quick sync — Acme pilot wants private deployment with HSM KMS and a 99.9% latency SLO. Need cross-team constraints: runtime, infra, security. Who owns the minimal path to ship and what are the blockers?
kevin: need model size + qps profile. are we shipping a 30B fp16 or a quantized 4-bit? impacts kernel selection and memory.
maya: @kevin they want 30B mixed-int8 quant for cost. ~120 reqs/min peak, 5% p95 spikes. target first public pilot in 6 weeks.
jasmin: VPC peering + private control plane — we need two infra slots in staging and one in prod. also certs for the customer domain. timeline wise, 3w to provision infra if nothing else blocks.
oliver: security checklist: threat model, HSM attestation, audit logging retention. HSM onboarding + compliance review is usually 4w. we can fast-track if infra & runtime agree on a narrow attack surface.
liam: capacity note: for 30B quant on a T4-like node we need pinned GPU per-tenant for steady SLO. prewarm window ~30s per model instance. autoscale policy needs warm pool.
nina: sequencing idea: 1) infra provision (staging) 2) runtime integration (quant kernels + prewarm) 3) security review + HSM test 4) canary 2 days -> 1w ramp. owners: infra:@jasmin, runtime:@kevin, security:@oliver, pm:@maya, sres:@liam.
maya: ok — can we compress HSM path? customer insists on using their KMS-backed HSM.
oliver: we can parallelize the attestation tests with runtime work but cannot skip audit steps. propose 2-week parallel window with a gating checklist: key rotation test, access mapping, tamper-evidence logs.
kevin: runtime risk: quant kernels for that model need a small follow-up patch to our batching layer to avoid KV-cache invalidation under concurrent tenants. dev time ~6-8 days + 2 days perf run.
jasmin: infra blocker: network ACLs for private control plane require security approvals. I'll kick off the ticket today. ETA 5 business days if approvals come back fast.
liam: SRE ops: recommend prewarm pool of 3 instances per customer to hit p95 target during spikes. cost tradeoff: +30% infra for steady state.
maya: tradeoff accepted for pilot. can you put numbers in a short runbook? link to our cost model doc: https://redwood.internal/finance/pilot-costs (private).
liam: will do, will post in this thread by EOD tomorrow.
nina: launch criteria (proposal): 1) staging e2e pass, 2) HSM attestation green, 3) p95 latency <= 300ms with prewarm, 4) rollback plan & canary policy, 5) runbook and oncall owner assigned.
kevin: can we get a reduced-scope fallback where if HSM delayed we use customer-managed KMS-on-VM for pilot only? needs security signoff.
oliver: we can allow a temporary KMS proxy for pilot with strict timebox + compensating controls. need explicit customer sign-off and risk acceptance.
maya: ok add fallback path to scope: KMS-proxy timed 30 days max. update owners.
jasmin: provisioning ticket: INF-4821 created. linking docs and assigning @kevin for runtime IPs.
deploy-bot: Deploy schedule precheck: staging slot available 2024-06-12. Marked tentative.
kevin: i'll land kernel patch branch today: `git checkout -b runtime/quant-kv-fix` then open PR.
liam: small ops ask: can runtime expose a /healthz? We need readiness signals before load balancer attaches.
kevin: yep will add `/healthz` + `/_prewarm_status`. simple JSON.
nina: decision log for roadmap: pilot ship window keeps 6-week target if infra approval within 5 business days and HSM attestation starts in parallel. else fallback KMS proxy path pushes to 8 weeks.
maya: action items recap: jasmin -> infra provisioning (INF-4821) (due 5bd); kevin -> kernel patch + /healthz (due 8 days); oliver -> fast-track HSM attestation kickoff (due 2w); liam -> runbook + cost numbers (EOD tomorrow); nina -> canary & rollback policy doc (due 4bd). please ack. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack. :thumbsup:
jasmin: ack, starting ticket. :eyes:
oliver: ack, will start attestation contact.
liam: ack, compiling runbook.
nina: ack, drafting canary policy.
maya: thanks all — we'll reconvene Wed for a quick checkpoint. if any blocker pops, ping #product on escalation.
